# Build: axf-data-postgres-real-tables-own

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-15T15:12:29.907Z
> Yeah, I want to migrate everything to a database in its own container. Land it, and then follow it up with Postgres.

## What to build
Continue build "axf-data on Postgres: real tables in its own container" (axf-data-postgres-real-tables-own) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-15 15:12):
"Yeah, I want to migrate everything to a database in its own container. Land it, and then follow it up with Postgres."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (1 left, ~10 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Follow-up to data-container-axf-data-holds-all (PR #704, SQLite + blobs). Move axf-data onto Postgres (Brett's Nov 6 choice) as its own private Coolify container with a persistent volume and daily backups. Real tables (not JSON copies or SQLite blobs) for: builds store, journal and history, notes, settings, planner items, UI reviews, the one true feature store, the Shipped features ledger, chats, and the API/control registry (apps/console-web/src/control/inventory.json becomes a table generated from each plugin's registered targets, never hand-edited, so builds stop clashing on it). Keep the data-store@1 API on top so callers don't change. Migrate from the SQLite axf-data with backup first, count checks, shadow, then cutover; never lose data. Tests, help, Shipped features. Land with the one-at-a-time lander.
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step axf-data-postgres-real-tables-own <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link axf-data-postgres-real-tables-own --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step axf-data-postgres-real-tables-own <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note axf-data-postgres-real-tables-own "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

Running `test_pg.py` by hand with `AXF_DATA_PG_TOOLS="docker exec -i <c>"`: `AXF_DATA_PG_TOOLS_DSN` is the container's own port (127.0.0.1:5432), not the mapped host port (noted in the test header).

VPS install after the merge: `sudo bash deploy/install-data.sh` (fresh: Postgres from the start), re-run the console installer, then migrate and shadow one namespace at a time (settings first, builds last) with `axf data mode`.
Shipped features ledger and Chat viewer still write SQLite locally; Postgres holds their rows as a mirror. Moving those plugins onto rows through data-store@1 (or a row API) is a follow-up.
UI Review: nothing new; #704's Data store tab layouts still wait for Brett.
